summary: Private 1981 light on a bluff at Port Ulao, Grafton, Wisconsin, built by a couple beside their home; Congress funded a Port Ulao light in 1850, never built.

light.note: Focal plane 163 feet (about 50 m) above the lake (LighthouseFriends, realtor.com). The characteristic is the station record's Light List entry; LighthouseFriends describes four seconds on and four off, WMHS describes eight and eight.

structures.note: White cylindrical tower, 50 feet tall, attached to the house (WMHS, LighthouseFriends, realtor.com). Wikipedia gives 40 feet above the bluff; not used.

access.note: Not open to the public. WMHS asks visitors not to go onto the grounds. The USLHS record says Open to Public: No.

facts.agency: Private owners (house and light). Current status per 2026 listing sources: for sale, under contingent offer; buyer not named. The Coast Guard lists it as a Class II private aid to navigation, light number 20765, certified 1990; the USLHS record disagrees (Private Aid: No).

events.note: Before the station existed: Congress appropriated $3,500 for a lighthouse at Port Ulao on 28 September 1850 (LighthouseFriends). The realtor.com article says the light was never built with public money.
Before the station existed: Congress allocated $1,000 on 3 August 1854 for a 'small beacon light on or near the pier at Port Ulao'. LighthouseFriends says it was never constructed.
Built by Brana Kevich, an Orthodox priest, and his wife Neva, attached to their home.
USLHS 'Year Established: 1981'; LighthouseFriends and Wikipedia give 1981 for the light.
Certified by the Coast Guard as a Class II private aid to navigation, light number 20765.

Sold to the next owning family in 1995 or 1996. LighthouseFriends gives 1995 in one passage ('In 1995, David and Mary Bennett purchased the property from the Keviches') and 1996 in another ('In 1996, Dave and Mary Bennett purchased the lighthouse'); WMHS says 1996; realtor.com says 1995. The buyers are not named in the story.

Listed for sale at $1.28 million, after about three decades with one family (LighthouseFriends). The realtor.com article, which LighthouseFriends dates to 12 August 2026, says it was already under contingent offer less than a month after listing. Buyer and listing agent not named.

notes_for_editor: THIN RECORD: no keepers, no storms, no wrecks and no primary government record of this light were found. The story's three chapters rest on LighthouseFriends, WMHS (December 2025), a realtor.com listing article and the USLHS record. NAMES: the builders (Brana and Neva Kevich) are named in their public role as the sources print them (WMHS and LighthouseFriends name them as builders; the story gives 'an Orthodox priest' only, because the sources disagree on the church). The 1995/1996 buyers (named in LighthouseFriends and in the realtor.com article) and the listing agent are NOT named. The 2026 status is given without a buyer. DISAGREEMENTS, all stated in the story or here: (1) Sale year: LighthouseFriends gives 1995 in one passage and 1996 in another (its cached page has both); WMHS 1996; realtor.com 1995. (2) Light timing: LighthouseFriends four seconds on and four off; WMHS eight and eight; the Light List's 'Iso W 8s' entry was not read. (3) Structure height: 50 feet in LighthouseFriends, WMHS and realtor.com; 40 feet above the bluff in Wikipedia, which is not cited. The station record's 15.0 m matches the three. (4) Church: LighthouseFriends and WMHS say Serbian Orthodox; realtor.com says Russian Orthodox; the story says only 'Orthodox'. (5) USLHS record: Active Aid to Navigation No and Private Aid No, which disagrees with the Coast Guard listing, LighthouseFriends ('continues to serve as an official aid to navigation') and WMHS ('functioning light'); the story reports both. (6) 'Highest focal plane': LighthouseFriends says only Boyer Bluff Light is higher among active Great Lakes lights; WMHS says it is the highest focal plane of any Great Lakes lighthouse; the story attributes the claim to LighthouseFriends. (7) Home completion: realtor.com says the house was constructed in 1977 and the light completed in 1981; the story says only that the light was built in 1981. DATES: realtor.com's cached copy is undated; LighthouseFriends refers to the same article (author Tiffani Sherman) as of 12 August 2026 and says the property was listed in 2026 and was already under contingent offer. The story uses that date through LighthouseFriends. The article's title in the cache differs slightly from the title LighthouseFriends cites. NOT CHECKED: the 1850 and 1854 congressional acts (not in the local corpus, which holds nothing for Port Ulao). A Chronicling America search for 'Port Ulao' in 1849-1856 returned 13 pages, none read. The station record's range (20 nautical miles) is from the Light List and is not repeated in the story. PHOTOS: the station record has no photos; none added. Wikipedia was read for leads only and is not cited.
